title: Call surface fidelity audit and rollback plan
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Problem: Customers are seeing intermittent failures and semantically incorrect outputs when using OpenAI-style tool descriptors against Redwood's legacy function surface. Root causes we've identified include: (1) parameter naming mismatches (snake_case vs camelCase), (2) optional vs required field semantics encoded differently across clients, (3) streaming chunk boundaries that split JSON-structured tool outputs, and (4) provenance/trace metadata being dropped by intermediate proxies. This ticket scopes an audit to quantify the mismatch surface, a minimal runtime reconciliation layer to fix common cases deterministically, and a rollback plan to revert changes safely if we observe regressions in quality or latency.

Goal: Ship a narrowly-scoped, reversible runtime change (no more than ~5 engineering points) that: (a) normalizes common argument name variants, (b) preserves structured outputs across streaming boundaries, (c) adds stable provenance headers to tool invocations, and (d) emits telemetry and perf counters so we can detect regressions and quantify customer impact. We will avoid broad compatibility heuristics; the focus is high recall for the most common failure classes and strong observability so we can iterate quickly.

Success metrics (initial):
- Reduction in customer-reported tool-call failures by 60% for the top 10 customers within 2 weeks of rollout.
- No more than 5% P95 tail latency regression on tool-call paths at peak.
- Clear telemetry that attributes: normalized fields applied, streaming-reassembly events, provenance header injection, and rollback-trigger counters.

Out of scope: Full canonical mapper for every possible tool schema, automatic shape inference for arbitrary nested parameter bags, and UI-level product changes (these will be tracked in follow-ups).
comments: 2026-03-02: Initial triage and signal review. Priya Desai ran log sweep across last 90 days and produced a list of 23 unique parameter name variants correlated with failures (link: https://go.redwood/confluence/call-fidelity-audit).

2026-03-04: Spike completed. Liam O'Connor validated a streaming reassembly approach that uses JSON-safe chunk buffering and emits a 'chunk-complete' sentinel to downstream parsers. Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2198

2026-03-07: Design sync with DX and Product. Agreed to add a provenance header 'X-RW-Invocation-Id' and include a minimal schema map for top 12 tools. Product recommends feature flag gating and gradual rollout (10% -> 50% -> 100%).

2026-03-10: Security reviewed the provenance header approach; no sensitive data will be included. They requested an opt-out flag for customers who cannot persist invocation IDs. Security note in Confluence: https://go.redwood/security/call-provenance

2026-03-13: Benchmarks run on staging cluster (n2-heavy). Observed 2.4% median latency uplift with single-threaded path, mitigated to 0.8% using fast-path bypass for already-canonical payloads. Telemetry hooks verified in staging.
decisions: Implement deterministic name canonicalization instead of probabilistic fuzzy matching: map a curated list of variants to canonical param names (e.g., 'user_id', 'userId', 'user-id' -> 'user_id').

Use a streaming reassembly buffer limited to 8KB per invocation to rejoin fragmented JSON outputs; if buffer overflow occurs, fall back to best-effort streaming passthrough and emit a telemetry event.
Inject X-RW-Invocation-Id at ingress and propagate through internal RPCs; persist to logs and event payloads for debugging and future tracing.
Gate the runtime change behind a config-driven feature flag and rollout via Canary -> Ramp -> Full using existing rollout automation in the console.
Provide a single-step rollback by flipping the feature flag; ensure telemetry includes rollback reasons and counts.
